html:
Sikkim is a small Himalayan kingdom between Nepal and Bhutan, ruled by the Namgyal dynasty from 1642 to 1975. On the 1815 map it is about to come under British protection.

Tradition says three Tibetan lamas crowned Phuntsog Namgyal as the first Chogyal, or religious king, at Yuksom in 1642. The kingdom was Buddhist and closely tied to Tibet, though most of its early people were Lepcha. It fought Bhutan, and from the 1770s the Gorkha kingdom of Nepal seized much of its land.

Britain backed Sikkim against Nepal in the Anglo-Nepalese War of 1814 to 1816, and the Treaty of Titalia in 1817 gave back lost land. In 1835 the Chogyal granted Darjeeling to the British. Sikkim became a British protectorate in 1861 and an Indian one in 1950. In 1975 its monarchy was abolished and it joined India as a state.
sum: Sikkim is a small Himalayan kingdom between Nepal and Bhutan, ruled by the Namgyal dynasty from 1642 to 1975. On the 1815 map it is about to come under British protection.
